solution.what: Grepped Tomokiyo's spanish2C page cache for R9959: Renard, 19 Feb 1554, Estado 808 f. 184, cipher = Granvelle-Saint Mauris PP1, opening 'Monsieur ... puis mes dernieres lectres'.

Fetched the 6 DECODE images with the stored cookie; address leaf reads 'Monseigneur le prince d'Espaigne' (recipient Philip, not Charles V as Tomokiyo heads it) and an archivist's note 'creo está descifrada en el nº 21'.
British History Online, CSP Spain XII, Feb 1554 16-20: 'Simon Renard to Prince Philip', 19 Feb, Simancas E. 808, Spanish translation, ~650 words, opening 'Since I last wrote' = the cipher's opening.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): linked the CSP Spain XII calendar text (Tyler 1949) by URL; no transcription of the ciphertext and no local copy of the decipherment

Full-texts audit (section I): tried to reach the cipher of R9959 for a transcription. Nothing in the folder under another name; DECODE public API and record page: no transcription or attachment; full-size images return the 'Insufficient permissions to see the full image' placeholder without a login (thumbnails only); PARES answered 429 Too Many Requests. Recorded transcription_missing; nothing transcribed.

outcome.method_basis: The contemporary Spanish decipherment is calendared in CSP Spain XII (Tyler 1949, 19 Feb 1554, Simancas E. 808) and Tomokiyo's spanish2C page identifies the key (PP1) and reads the opening; both were found before any work on the cipher, and nothing was transcribed or deciphered here.
outcome.notes: Calendared 1949 from the contemporary Spanish decipherment; key published (PP1); catalogue entry 202 removed, no write-up.

texts.label: R9959, 19 Feb 1554
texts.summary: Simon Renard in London to Prince Philip, 19 February 1554: French plots discovered show that Courtenay and the Lady Elizabeth, through Peter Carew, Wyatt, Crofts and Lord Thomas Grey, conspired to throw the Queen of England into the Tower; the powers sent by way of France have come and the Pope has granted a dispensation.
texts.note: Decryption: the English calendar text (Royall Tyler, CSP Spain XII, 1949, pp. 100-123) of the Spanish version of the contemporary decipherment; a modern edition, linked, not copied. The decipherment itself ('no. 21' in AGS E. 808) was not located and the French plaintext not rebuilt. No transcription of the ciphertext (DECODE images not transcribed).
